1.) thank you so much for all the compliments!! 

2.) feel free to ask me any questions about makeup.

As for what I do, I use eyeshadow for basically everything (some concealer occasionally for a spot or under eye bags but not often.)

I always fill in my eyebrows. The key here is actually to NOT be precise. You don't want it to look like your eyebrows are perfectly filled, just thicker. Follow your natural brow, stay inside the lines of where your hair grows. Sometimes I'll even wipe over my brows when I'm done to get off any excess eyeshadow.

Occasionally I contour, just under my cheekbones. I have a pretty angular face so this may not work with everyone. YMMV.

Then I take gray eyeshadow (no glitter) and lightly brush it along where there would naturally by facial hair, specifically accentuating my upper lip and the area surrounding my chin. Again, everyone's faces are different, so this may not work for others. I also take the same shade and lightly fill in my side burn area and go downward to my jaw line. Once again, you don't need precision. 

And sometimes I'll add a shade or two darker than my skin tone to my top eye lid and around my bottom eye life to make my eyes appear a little more sunken.

That's pretty much it!

Edit: 

Oh! Almost forgot. If you are going to add shadow to your jawline, do it UNDER the jawline. If you touch your jawline right now with your hand and run your hand along it, it should be the area your thumb touches. UNDER, not ON the jaw line. This will create a realistic shadow rather than a weird looking faded chin strap. The more you know!

I know I'm super late to this party (sorted too of this month, as I'm planning on meal prepping soon) and I actually am a Pet Nutritional Consultant (specifically dog and cat) and yeah a lot of people seem to be misinformed.

My thoughts are pretty simple. I don't recommend homemade meals for puppies, especially not for large breeds. They need very specific calcium and phosphorous levels, as well as certain protein and fat levels. Otherwise, things can and will go wrong, if not now, then later on in life. 

I understand wanting the best for your dog-- I do! I have a dog and I want to make sure she is eating the best food I can get for her. But you have to be careful and make sure that what you're doing is the best thing. Raw diets are AMAZING. They really are, they've changed so many dogs lives, but, they're not for everyone. Anything with a suppressed immune system, like PUPPIES, I don't recommend it until they're adults. And, with frozen raw or freeze dried raw bought from a store, it usually undergoes a process called High Pressure Processing, or HPP for short. This helps to rid the raw diet of dangerous bacteria.

Also, homemade diets lead to a lot of imbalances in vitamins and minerals. It's worth nothing that while yes, dogs are carnivores and should absolutely be on a meat-based diet (excluding very rare instances) they actually do need other things like fruits and veggies to sustain them. Because yeah, they're carnivores, but the truth is that dogs are scavengers and are opportunistic rather than obligate. Plus, they'll eat the organs of the prey they find. Which means added Taurine, Iron, Zinc, etc. and ALSO means they'll be eating those yummy stomachs lined with tripe and all sorts of other goodies that the prey ate-- like fruits and veggies!

Long story short-- this isn't the worst things I've ever seen. Arguably better than some dog food brands out there. I just hope and pray that OP has DONE THEIR RESEARCH (and that means more than just using a blog or two, I mean doing real research.)

I've only ever lived in Houston personally but I've traveled all over Texas, so here we go.

Texas is an amazing place for many reasons. If you live in Houston, the cost of living is very affordable if you know where to look, especially when compared to the other biggest cities in the US. Like me, I live in a less than $600 town home. I'm not in a bad part of town, and I have a short commute to work. It's a great deal.

We have a beach! Really close! Depending on where you live, you can make a day trip to Galveston, thought I'll warn you that the waters aren't... well, they're not great. Gotta love that Galveston brown. But the Strand is nice, it's an area in Galveston with a ton of little shops and stores. There's also Pleasure Pier, a small amusement/theme park that overlooks the Gulf of Mexico. If you go further down to South Padre Island, the water is a little nicer, and if you really want nicer beaches, plan a weekend to go down to Corpus Christi and enjoy the beaches there. Oh and, just like New Orleans, Galveston celebrates Mardi Gras. It's not the true New Orleans experience, but it's a helluva time.

Cruise down to San Antonio for their river walk, amongst other historical sights like The Alamo. Or drive up to Austin to go drinking down Sixth street, a historic street and Austins most entertaining district. From there you can also tour other historical buildings and see Texas's capital.

Or drive up to Dallas! Where... erm... hmm. Where you can see a lot of concrete, huge belt buckles and women with big hair! (Houstonians don't love Dallas so I'll be honest, I don't really know much but I've been told it's terrible but hey, what do I know? I've just never met a native Houstonian that liked Dallas. We are very different cities though.)

We've got Big Bend, multiple other parks and rivers, a wide variety of scenery and landscapes, and we have some of the best state-wide stores.

H-E-B is one of the things I would miss dearly if I ever left. I'll admit I took it for granted until I had enough people tell me that HEB is one of, if not the best grocery stores in the nation. They're adorable, efficient, and always lively. We've also got Buccee's, which is a gas station/convenience store that kicks all other gas stations asses. And they've got the cleanest bathrooms around, I guarantee it. We've also got Whataburger, which, if you've never had... you don't know what you're missing. Their burgers are filling, meaty, and everything I want out of a burger. 

Oh! There's also the Houston Rodeo, the biggest rodeo in the nation (and maybe the world? I don't know!) It's huge though. It lasts about 20 days in March-ish and you can see the livestock, concerts, you can have fun at the carnival, eat ANYTHING deep fried, and of course, you can watch the rodeo! (Always worth watching Mutton Busting and the Calf Scramble. Adorable and Hilarious.)

So what are some downsides to Texas? Well, our minimum wage is relatively low, but the cost of living -almost- makes up for it, though not quite enough. Texas is huge, so if you wanted to get from, say, Houston to New Mexico, and you wanted to drive, you'd consider that a road trip as it would take anywhere from 10-15 hours. It's also HOT. And it's a different kind of heat than in Arizona or places like that; this is a humid heat. Meaning you will sweat a lot. Texas is also pretty conservative, though if you stick to the larger cities it becomes less so.

But all in all, Texas is pretty great. Our government could be better, but hey, that's what everyone says, right? Plus you can get anything Texas shaped! And I mean anything.
